prompt:
Artificial intelligence is changing the way software systems are designed and deployed.
Large language models use transformer architectures to process sequences of tokens and generate predictions.
Modern AI infrastructure requires efficient inference systems that can provide low latency and high throughput.
GPU memory, batching, scheduling, quantization, and hardware utilization all affect inference performance.
Large language model serving systems must balance response latency with aggregate throughput.
Interactive applications usually care about time to first token while large batch workloads often prioritize total generated tokens per second.
Performance benchmarking requires controlled workloads so different systems can be compared fairly.
The model, hardware, input length, output length, concurrency, and

benchmark methodology should remain consistent across experiments.
Deep learning models rely heavily on matrix operations executed across specialized accelerators such as tensor cores and vector processing units.
Optimizing memory bandwidth and cache locality is paramount for achieving peak operational intensity during the auto-regressive decode phase.
Distributed inference techniques including tensor parallelism and pipeline parallelism enable serving models that exceed the capacity of a single device.
